title: Hall's children and grandchildren
summary: His children's careers, grandchildren, and the 1950 separation from his second wife.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What are your children doing? Are any of them musically inclined or connected musically?

Well, they're not connected musically. Barbara is working for a hospital. She's a Senior Health Program Analyst for the mental health hospitals of all New York, and she has a daughter, Linda, 17, still going to school, on scholarship.

And Alfred is in Wall Street. He's a consultant, analyst-consultant. And Nancy was a New York Times reporter, Nancy Hicks. She married Bob Maynard, who was a Washington Post -- maybe you know him? Well, they live in Washington, So they quit their papers, and they're putting out a journal for ethnic groups, and they have a summer school program in Berkeley in the summer.
How many grandchildren do you have, just the one?
No. Barbara has one. Alfred has two,
Kim and Dana, 10 and 5 years old, and David is 7. That's Nancy's son. And she has a stepdaughter of 18 years old now. She --
Well, that's -- that's that part of it.
So, and I knocked about a while doing the various things.
When did you and your second wife part?
In 1950. And I did a lot of different things as far as playing during that period.
